Write a polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Independent Set and TARGET is Clique. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

SOURCE = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;

  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique.

An independent set in G is exactly a clique in the complement graph of G,
so the reduction keeps n and k unchanged and replaces the edge list by the
complement edge list.  Building the complement takes O(n^2) time.
"""

from itertools import combinations


def reduce(instance):
    """Map an IndependentSet instance to a Clique instance.

    Instance format (both problems):
        {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

    The complement graph has an edge between u and v exactly when the
    original graph does not.  A set of vertices is independent in the
    original graph iff it is a clique in the complement, so the yes/no
    answer is preserved, including the k <= 0 and k > n edge cases.
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]
    original = {frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in instance["edges"]}
    complement_edges = [
        [u, v]
        for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2)
        if frozenset((u, v)) not in original
    ]
    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": k}
EOF

"""Tests comparing brute-force answers on source instances and reductions."""

import random

import problems
from problems import IndependentSet, Clique
from reduce import reduce


def check(instance):
    IndependentSet.validate(instance)
    reduced = reduce(instance)
    Clique.validate(reduced)
    expected = IndependentSet.is_yes(instance)
    got = Clique.is_yes(reduced)
    assert expected == got, (instance, reduced, expected, got)
    return 1


def main():
    tests_run = 0
    tests_passed = 0

    # Exhaustive small instances, including k = -1 and k = n + 1.
    for scale in range(0, 5):
        for instance in IndependentSet.enumerate_instances(scale):
            tests_run += 1
            check(instance)
            tests_passed += 1

    # Random instances, including edge-case k values.
    rng = random.Random(12345)
    for _ in range(3000):
        scale = rng.randint(0, 8)
        instance = IndependentSet.random_instance(rng, scale)
        tests_run += 1
        check(instance)
        tests_passed += 1

    # Hand-picked edge cases.

        {"n": 0, "edges": [], "k": -5},
